entities.text: Transfer Civil Miscellaneous Petition No.462 of 2024
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text:
Heard Sri K. Venumadhav, learned counsel for the transfer petitioner and Sri Naraparaju Avaneesh,
learned counsel for the respondent.
Perused the entire record.

2. This petition is filed under Section 24 of C.P.C. seeking transfer of F.C.O.P.No.449 of 2024 pending on the file of the Judge, Family Court at Hanumakonda, to the Court of the Judge, Family Court at Nizamabad.

3. The petitioner and respondent are wife and husband and are involved in matrimonial dispute,
whereby the petitioner filed DVC case in D.V.C.No.31 of 2024 and criminal case under Section 498-A and 420 of the IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961, and the same are pending before the Courts at Nizamabad.
The petitioner is residing with her parents at Nizamabad.
While so, the respondent has filed F.C.O.P.No.449 of 2024 in Hanumakonda seeking restitution of conjugal rights.
4. It is the case of the petitioner that the harassment meted out by the respondent is unbearable and there is no hope for reunion and she intends to file divorce petition at Nizamabad.

Since all the cases are pending at RY,J Tr.CMP_462_2024 Nizamabad and since it is convenient for her to prosecute all the cases filed by her at Nizamabad, sought for transfer of the F.C.O.P.No.449 of 2024 pending at Hanumakonda.
The remaining facts narrated relate to situations leading to filing of the criminal and DVC cases are not recounted.

5. The respondent filed detailed counter denying the allegations made by the petitioner in the present petition with respect to disputes leading to filing of the cases and the said allegations are not recounted as they are not necessary for the adjudication of this petition.

The respondent opposed the transfer petition expressing difficulty in engaging advocate from Nizamabad, Armoor, Nirmal and Metpally Bar Associations to contest the DVC as well as the criminal case as the father of the petitioner has influenced majority of the advocates.
The respondent was advised to engage an advocate either from Hanumakonda or from Hyderabad for effective prosecution of the case.

It is further pleaded that the father of the petitioner threatened the respondent and his family members that he will make DVC case listed with short durations to make the respondent and his family members to roam from Hanumakonda and Nizamabad until their demands are accepted.
The respondent is facing threat for attending the Courts at Nizamabad.
The respondent and his family members would suffer loss and hardship to attend the Courts at Nizamabad.
Further, it is RY,J Tr.CMP_462_2024 submitted that the F.C.O.P.No.449 of 2024 is filed at Hanumakonda, wherein the respondent and the petitioner last resided.
Therefore, opposed the prayer in the present petition.

sentences.text: Having regard to the allegations made by the petitioner, it is seen that the DVC and criminal case are registered in Nizamabad.

Further, the petitioner has expressed her intention to file F.C.O.P.
seeking divorce in the Family Court at Nizamabad.
The respondent and his family members have to attend the criminal case at Nizamabad.
The only case pending at Hanumakonda is F.C.O.P.No.449 of 2024.
The respondent opposed the present petition on the grounds of difficulty in engaging a counsel at Nizamabad and threat perception due to the influence of the father of the petitioner.
In any case, the respondent is attending the cases at Nizamabad and therefore, transfer of F.C.O.P.No.449 of 2024 to Nizamabad would facilitate trial of all the cases at Nizamabad.
The respondent may make request before respective Courts to list all the cases as per his convenience on the same day.
In case of any threat perception, the said matter can be reported to the police.
It is also difficult to conceive the scenario where no person from Nizamabad Bar Association would be willing to take up the case of the respondent.
The respondent being qualified medical RY,J Tr.CMP_462_2024 professional should have means to engage the counsel in Nizamabad or engage a counsel from Hanumakonda or Hyderabad.

7. In view of the foregoing discussion, this Court is of the considered opinion that while considering the convenience of the petitioner to prosecute the case filed by her and also on account of unsustainable reasons given by the respondent in opposing the transfer, the relief prayed for is granted.
8.

In the result, the Transfer Civil Miscellaneous Petition is allowed and the F.C.O.P.No.449 of 2024 pending on the file of the Judge, Family Court at Hanumakonda, is withdrawn and transferred to the Court of the Judge, Family Court at Nizamabad.

entities.text: Court of the Judge, Family Court at Nizamabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The entire original record shall be transmitted within a period of one month.
There shall be no order as to costs.

Miscellaneous Petitions, if any,
pending in this petition, shall stand closed.
